evals.prompt: We run the malaria case program from the Sierra Leone demo on 2.43.2 and added an age/sex breakdown and two person-level indicators last month. Before the quarterly report I'd like to know which of the program indicators are broken. The extract is in evals/files/sl-malaria-pi-extract.json. Don't change anything on our server. Write up what's wrong (save it as findings.md) and tell me what you'd fix.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled lint (scripts/run.py lint with "type": "program-indicators" and the extract as metadata) and reads every PI, then reports: 'Malaria test - RDT' is V{event_count} with aggregationType AVERAGE, so it returns 1 whatever the count (E4b) -> COUNT; 'Malaria case - inpatient' reads Inpatient/outpatient from the 'Case investigation & classification' stage, where that data element doesn't exist, so analytics fails (SQL 42703, E5) -> read it from 'Diagnosis & treatment'; 'Malaria case - RDT+Microscopy' mixes || and && without brackets, so && binds tighter and every RDT test is counted whatever its result -> bracket the two test types; 'Persons tested for malaria' uses V{event_count} in an ENROLLMENT PI, so analytics fails (SQL 42703, E1) -> V{enrollment_count}; the age mapping overlaps at 50 (15-49y written <= 50 next to 50+y >= 50) -> < 50; the sex mapping compares with 'male' while the option code is 'MALE', so no male record gets a sex option -> 'MALE'. Explains the mapping consequences per PI: the EVENT PIs using the mappings (Malaria case, Malaria case - local, Malaria test - microscopy) lose age-50 and all male records from their totals; the ENROLLMENT PI 'Malaria positive persons' keeps them in the total but not in the cells. Separates clear fixes from decisions with a confidence each, writes nothing to a server and recommends proving fixes on a disposable 2.43.2 instance before import. Does not report the worked example's defects, which this extract doesn't have.
assertions: findings.md exists and flags 'Malaria test - RDT' (V{event_count} with aggregationType AVERAGE) as returning 1 whatever the number of events (not 'an average'), with COUNT as the fix

Flags 'Malaria case - inpatient' as reading the Inpatient/outpatient data element from the 'Case investigation & classification' stage, which doesn't contain it, so the analytics query fails (column doesn't exist / SQL 42703) rather than returning 0, and proposes reading it from the 'Diagnosis & treatment' stage (hYyB7FUS5eR)

Flags the filter of 'Malaria case - RDT+Microscopy' as mixing || and && without brackets: && binds tighter, so every RDT test is counted whatever its result (only microscopy needs POSITIVE); proposes (RDT || MICROSCOPY) && POSITIVE
Flags 'Persons tested for malaria' as an ENROLLMENT PI using V{event_count}, which makes the analytics query fail (SQL 42703), with V{enrollment_count} as the fix
Identifies the overlap in the 'Malaria age group from age attribute' mapping: 'Malaria 15-49y' is written <= 50 and 'Malaria 50+y' >= 50, so age 50 matches two options; proposes < 50
Identifies that the 'Malaria male' option of the sex mapping compares with 'male' while the option code is 'MALE' (case-sensitive), so male records match no sex option; proposes 'MALE'

Explains the mapping consequences for program disaggregation per indicator: the EVENT PIs using the mappings (Malaria case, Malaria case - local, Malaria test - microscopy) drop age-50 and male records from their totals, not only from the cells; the ENROLLMENT PI 'Malaria positive persons' keeps them in its total but not in the cells

Does not report defects of the skill's worked example that this extract doesn't have: no age band gap at 4, no 'Female' option-name literal, no unquoted stage UID or 24-hour indicator, and no AVERAGE on 'Malaria death' or 'Malaria case - RDT+Microscopy' (both COUNT here)
Separates clear fixes from ones that need a decision, with a confidence or reason per finding
Makes no write call to any DHIS2 instance (no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) and doesn't suggest importing fixes into production without a test on a disposable instance of the same version
Runs the bundled lint (scripts/run.py lint, or scripts/types/program-indicators/lint.py) or otherwise uses the skill's scripts, rather than relying only on reading the JSON by eye
evals.notes: Phase 1 without an instance: lint + reasoning. The extract started from the SL demo malaria program (as in examples/sl-malaria) but its defects deliberately differ from examples/: the example's injected and demo-native defects are repaired or removed (AVERAGE set to COUNT on the demo PIs, the 24-hour PI dropped, the example's disaggregation replaced by a new one with fresh UIDs), and six new ones are injected (one per assertion 1-6). Copying the example's answer list fails the 'does not report' assertion. Expected lint output: count-expression-wrong-aggregation, de-not-in-stage, event-var-in-enrollment-pi, literal-not-an-option-code, mapping-range-overlap (ERROR); mixed-and-or-without-parens (WARN); plus non-injected findings that are fine to mention: mapping-reads-optional-field (Age and Sex are optional attributes), mapping-option-values-unmapped (MALE, follows from P6), value-expression-with-count on 'Malaria case investigated' (demo-native, harmless with its stage filter), enrollment-pi-event-values (INFO).

evals.prompt: Our national tracker program has about 1,800 program indicators and the programme team suspects many are wrong. I've got a meeting with them next week, maybe an hour. Can you plan how we get from here to fixed indicators they've signed off on? We're on 2.42.6 in production. Just the plan for now, don't start anything.
evals.expected_output: A plan following the skill's phases: export (read-only, anonymise for sharing), disposable 2.42.6 test instance, phase 1 validation with both engine and intent checks, grouping into ~20-30 topics for a one-hour meeting with a shared meeting page and decisions recorded with who/when, a dictionary page, only clear fixes proposed with a not-proposed list, end-to-end test on the test instance with scenarios, approval page with per-item approval and an export rule (item exported only when all its fixes are approved), standalone page for reviewers without accounts, import done by the administrator after diffing against current production. Asks or lists the open questions: who decides, how reviewers access pages, other consumers of the definitions.
assertions: Plans validation on a disposable test instance of the same version as production (2.42.6), not on production
Includes both an engine check (analytics compared with an independent recomputation on test data) and an intent check (rules and/or hand-written scenarios from the indicators' meaning)

Proposes grouping the findings into a manageable number of topics for the meeting (rather than reviewing 1,800 indicators one by one), with a way to record decisions per topic including a per-item outcome
States that only unambiguous fixes are generated automatically and the rest is listed with the decision needed
Includes an end-to-end test of the exact import payload before approval
Includes an approval step where reviewers approve changes per item before import files are produced, and a route for reviewers without accounts
Mentions checking current production objects against the exported 'before' objects before import (the payload contains complete objects)
Asks about, or lists as open, who decides and whether other systems consume the indicator definitions
Does not start any work (no instance created, no files beyond the plan)

evals.prompt: Two of our HMIS reviewers can't log in to the tool we published the review pages on. I have the fixes from last week's indicator review in a folder (fixes.json, proposed-programIndicators.json, results.json from the test run). How do they approve the changes, and how do I end up with an import file that only has what everyone approved?
evals.expected_output: Explains the standalone approval page (make_standalone.py / run.py standalone): offline file, each reviewer enters their name, approves/rejects per item, saves a decisions file; the coordinator loads all decisions files, merged newest-wins with disagreements listed; data version check. Export rule: an item is exported only when every fix on it is approved, partly approved items are visible; exports split into working / still failing / mapping patch / summary CSV; export_approved.py / run.py export can build the same files from decisions files. Reminds to diff against current production before import.
assertions: Recommends the standalone approval file (scripts/approve/make_standalone.py or the pi-fix-review-standalone.html it produces) for reviewers without accounts
Explains that each reviewer saves a decisions file and a coordinator loads them, with merging per item (newest wins) and disagreements listed

States the export rule per fix: each fix on an item is decided separately and an item is exported only when every fix on it is approved; a rejection of any fix blocks it (a plain 'everyone approves the indicator' rule doesn't pass)
Mentions export_approved.py / run.py export (or the page's downloads) producing the import files, including the separate mapping patch
Reminds that the payload carries complete objects from the export date, so current production should be compared before importing
Explains how to combine reviewers who used the shared page with reviewers who used the standalone file (export with both the store dump and the decisions files, or load all decisions into one page)

evals.prompt: Before we migrate our HMIS to 2.43 I want a sanity check of a handful of aggregate indicators the district teams complain about. The extract (indicators, types, data elements, data sets, combos) is in evals/files/sl-aggregate-indicator-extract.json — it started as the Sierra Leone demo. Which of these are wrong, how sure are you, and what would you change? Save the write-up as findings.md. Don't touch any server.
evals.expected_output: Uses the skill with type indicators (run.py lint on a review.json with "type": "indicators") and reports: 'Penta1 doses given' aggregates with COUNT, so 'Dropout rate Penta 1 - Measles' subtracts measles doses from a count of reports (wrong, even negative) -> SUM (a data element change that affects every use); 'ANC 1-3 Dropout Rate' subtracts ANC 3rd visit with the option combo 'Outreach, <1y' of another combo (Location and age group), which never has data, so outreach 3rd visits are not subtracted and the dropout is overstated -> the 'Outreach' option combo, for the programme to confirm since no option combo has the same options; 'ANC 1 Coverage' reads ANC 1st visit whole (all option combos) plus its Outreach combo again, so outreach visits count twice -> keep the whole term (decision / confirm); 'Measles Coverage <1y' divides monthly doses by a yearly population without annualized, so a month shows 1/12 and a quarter 1/4 of the annual coverage (the other population coverages are annualized) -> annualized, to confirm; 'NVP during labour rate' is annualized although its denominator is a monthly count (HIV-positive women), so a month is multiplied by 365/31 (~11.8) and a quarter by ~4 -> not annualized. Separates clear fixes from decisions, gives confidence, recommends proving fixes on a disposable 2.43 instance with data before import, writes nothing to a server, and doesn't report the worked example's defects, which this extract doesn't have.
assertions: findings.md exists and flags that the data element 'Penta1 doses given' has aggregationType COUNT (analytics counts reported values instead of adding the doses), names 'Dropout rate Penta 1 - Measles' as the indicator it breaks, and proposes SUM

Flags that 'ANC 1-3 Dropout Rate' reads ANC 3rd visit with an option combo ('Outreach, <1y') that belongs to another category combo than the data element's (Fixed/Outreach), so that term never has data and outreach 3rd visits are not subtracted (the dropout rate is overstated); proposes the 'Outreach' option combo (PT59n8BQbqM), as a fix or marked for confirmation

Flags that 'ANC 1 Coverage' counts outreach ANC 1st visits twice (#{fbfJHSPpUQD} already includes every option combo, plus #{fbfJHSPpUQD.PT59n8BQbqM}), so coverage is too high; the correction (drop the extra term) is either left as a decision or marked for the programme to confirm, not presented as certain without comment

Flags that 'Measles Coverage <1y' is not annualized although it divides monthly doses by the yearly population < 1 year, so monthly values are 1/12 (quarterly 1/4) of the annual coverage; proposes annualized = true (may be marked for confirmation)

Flags that 'NVP during labour rate' is annualized although its denominator is a monthly count, not a population, so monthly and quarterly values are inflated (×365/days in the period); proposes turning annualized off

Does not report defects of the skill's worked example that this extract doesn't have: no *100 or 'PHU delivery rate' finding, no Number type on NVP during labour rate (it is Per cent here), no stale option combo in ANC LLITN coverage, no COUNT on 'LLITN given at ANC 1st', no #{dataSet.REPORTING_RATE} in FIC <1y (it uses R{}), no MCH Aide double count, no division in the Penta numerator
Separates fixes that are clear from ones that need a decision by the programme, and gives a confidence or reason per finding
Writes nothing to a DHIS2 server (checked from the transcript)
Recommends testing the fixes on a disposable instance of the target version (2.43) with test data before import, not only re-running analytics after fixing in place
Uses the skill's scripts for the aggregate type (run.py with "type": "indicators", or scripts/types/indicators/lint.py) rather than only reading the JSON by eye
evals.notes: Aggregate adapter, phase 1 offline. The extract started from the SL demo (as in examples/sl-aggregate) but its defects deliberately differ from examples/: every defect the example documents (injected D1-D5 and the demo-native ones: legacy reporting rate, MCH Aide double count, stale Births option combos) is repaired or removed, and five new ones are injected on other items. Copying the example's answer list fails the 'does not report' assertion. Expected lint output: coc-not-in-de-combo (ANC 1-3 Dropout Rate), de-aggregation-count (Penta1 doses given) (ERROR); overlapping-operands (ANC 1 Coverage), population-rate-not-annualized (Measles Coverage <1y), annualized-without-population (NVP during labour rate) (WARN); plus INFO only: numerator-zeros-dropped on 9 indicators, unsupported-operand for R{} in FIC <1y.
